title: Choose PressBig's visual world
question: Pick the look for pressbig.com: the lead direction, an alternate, or re-roll for a new hand.

options.label: The Contact Sheet
options.lineage: photographers' proof sheets and film-strip rebates
options.thesis: A daily edit you can see being picked: the day's stories as numbered frames with the best circled in red grease pencil.
options.viewport: A giant headline on the left; on the right one circled lead frame over a strip of four more, each numbered like film.
options.risk: A photographer's tool can read arty unless the headline and the red button stay loud and plain.

raised.raise: The whole site uses exactly four inks and never mixes a fifth.
Grease-pencil red is the only control and state colour, like the cape's single gold cord.
Picked, seen and new are marks (circle, tick, dot), never tints.
State prints itself as labels on the rebate: roll number, frame count, 'PICKED'.
Every roll label carries its edit date, like a dated jar label.

options.label: The Album Page
options.thesis: Today's edit is one album page of numbered slots, and every story is a foil sticker you collect.
options.viewport: Huge 'Fill today's page' headline beside a slot grid already holding four stickers, with a progress bar.
options.risk: Everyone knows it, so it can feel childlike; the stickers must carry grown-up headlines.

options.label: The Torn Hoarding
options.lineage: décollage: posters torn off a Paris hoarding
options.thesis: Each day's edit is a poster layer; pulling it back reveals yesterday's underneath.
options.viewport: Layers of torn sheets with a big 'Peel back the day' headline and a pull-tab to see yesterday.
options.case: Poster walls are pop culture's own surface, but torn fragments cost scan speed.
options.risk: Pretty chaos hides the stories; reading order must stay obvious.

options.label: Four-Shade Handheld
options.viewport: A 160x144 screen showing stories as tiles with a blinking cursor.
options.case: Great for gadgets and gaming nostalgia, but one type size and four greens cannot carry fashion or celebrity.
options.kept: A hard cap on the palette.
options.risk: Reads as a retro game, not a lifestyle site.

options.label: The Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: black silk cape with a gold drawcord
options.viewport: A black semicircle that gathers into pleats when a gold cord is pulled.
options.case: Elegant for fashion alone, but it excludes gadgets and mainstream readers.
options.kept: One accent colour as the only control.
options.risk: Fashion-snobby, which the brief rules out.

options.label: The Brine Calendar
options.viewport: A shelf of jars, each labelled with a harvest date and day count.
options.case: A calendar of dated jars suits a daily edit, but food imagery says nothing about entertainment or tech.
options.risk: Audience would not guess what the site is about.

options.label: The Emission Rail
options.lineage: spectrogram plates on a viewing box
options.viewport: Destinations as ticks on one off-centre rail, the open one blooming into a plate.
options.case: A scientific instrument tool; mainstream readers would not identify with it.
options.kept: State carried by form, not colour.
options.risk: Cold and technical, the opposite of fun.

options.label: The Midnight Terminal
options.viewport: One scrolling transcript of stories typed onto a dark screen.
options.case: A tool's costume for a media site; an 80-column transcript hides images and fashion.
options.kept: State prints itself as plain labels.
options.risk: Developer-toy feel for a mainstream audience.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean entertainment-and-lifestyle magazine homepage, executed with real craft.
canonCard.viewport: A hero story with three smaller picks beside it and a row of category tabs.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other lifestyle site by design.
